title: Aliasing and memory
description: Pointers, copies, and who owns heap data in C

exercises.title: String reassignment
exercises.description: Assign `s = "hi"`, assign `t = s`, print `t` with `print` (no newline).
hints: `const char *t = s;` copies the pointer; both refer to the same `"hi"` literal.
`printf("%s", t);` — no newline if the grader expects bare `hi`.

exercises.title: Slice header copy
exercises.description: Create `s = list[1, 2}`, assign `t = s`, set `t[0] = 9`, print `s[0]` and `s[1]` concatenated as digits with `print` (no space, no newline) → `92`.
hints: `int *t = s;` means `t` aliases the same storage as `s`.

exercises.title: Int copy
exercises.description: `a = 3`, `b = a`, increment `b` with `b++`, print `a` and `b` space-separated with `print` (no trailing newline).
hints: `int b = a;` copies the value; only `b++` changes `b`.
